title: Great app - missing critical feature
body: 3 stars for now. Great app - missing critical features to be truly usable. While it’s a great all in one application for most uses the lack of user definable locations makes it unusable for making weather calls at one or more locations if you’re either not physically preset there or don’t know the exact location from memory. Second is quad screen display mode on tablets. During severe weather events the less screens one has to switch the better off one is.Third is historical data mode for further analysis after an event. Fourth is no favorites to store multiple frequently accessed radar sites. $100/yr for an app that doesn’t have these abilities is frankly disappointing. WeatherWise, Radar Omega & Radar Scope all offer this functionality. The imagery is great, the UI could be a bit cleaner/more user friendly but I suspect that it would become easier with more frequent use.

title: Genuinely good, smooth app

title: New Best Free Radar/Satellite/Model App?
body: As someone who has been studying the weather and tracking it consistently for years now, it has been hard to find multiple good radar apps. Tracking tornadoes and hurricanes from a meteorological standpoint is completely different from using your normal precipitation map that people call the “radar.” As for actual radar apps, there’s really only a few that have dominated for years. This one just became a contender for that list in the first hour of its release. It has more features than any other free radar app on the market. In addition to this, you really can’t just call this a radar app. Yes, it has all of the radar features (with precipitation and velocity in super resolution) but it has so much more. It also has real time satellite data along with the GFS and HRRR weather models (hopefully more to come in the future). This is something that very few apps have and to my knowledge, this one does it better than any other. You can also overlay weather forecasts on top of all these things and with an amazing road map, I’d assume storm chasers will also gladly start using this. There isn’t a weather app I recommend more than this one!
